area: salesagent test harness & local run story (unified multi-transport dispatch, tenant/principal seeding, e2e live-server mode, Docker/agent-db standup, buyer auth)
summary: salesagent's test harness (tests/harness/) is a per-domain "Env" abstraction: each Env subclass declares EXTERNAL_PATCHES (what to mock) and implements four thin transport bridges — call_impl (direct _impl), call_a2a (real AdCPRequestHandler.on_message_send pipeline), call_mcp (in-memory FastMCP Client), and build_rest_body/parse_rest_response (FastAPI TestClient). BaseTestEnv.call_via(Transport, **kwargs) is the unified dispatcher: it injects the transport-correct ResolvedIdentity, routes to a per-transport Dispatcher class (dispatchers.py), and returns a frozen TransportResult carrying payload / wire_response / wire_error_envelope. This "same logical request across every transport" pattern is exactly what a buyer transport layer should mirror — one env method per wire, a single call_via front door, and a normalized result the tests assert against regardless of transport. Tenant/principal/products are created with factory-boy factories (tests/factories/) bound to a real session inside `with env:`; IntegrationEnv.setup_default_data() creates a Tenant+Principal, and in integration mode the harness commits factory rows and threads the Principal.access_token through the REAL auth chain (header x-adcp-auth → token→DB lookup → ResolvedIdentity). E2E mode (Transport.E2E_REST + RestE2EDispatcher) sends real HTTP via httpx to a live nginx→FastAPI→Postgres Docker stack, binding factories to the server's DB via E2EConfig.postgres_url so Given-step data is visible over the wire. Local standup is either the full dev stack (docker compose up → http://localhost:8000, auth token "test-token"/admin password test123) or, for integration tests, an isolated bare Postgres per worktree via the agent-db skill. A buyer client authenticates with an x-adcp-auth token (the Principal.access_token row) plus x-adcp-tenant (the tenant subdomain); the CI seed uses token "ci-test-token" in tenant subdomain "ci-test".
invariants: call_via always injects a transport-correct identity via kwargs.setdefault('identity', identity_for(transport)) — caller-supplied identity wins; identity=None is meaningful (no-auth / 401 path).

TransportResult is frozen: is_success == (error is None and payload is not None); is_error == (error is not None). wire_response populated on success (REST body / MCP structured_content / A2A artifact DataPart); wire_error_envelope populated on error from real wire bytes; both None on IMPL (no wire).

Error envelope is a two-layer dict {adcp_error:{code,message,recovery,details}, errors:[...]}; reconstruction (_envelope_to_adcp_error) is LOSSY (AdCPAuthentication vs AdCPAuthorization both map to AUTH_REQUIRED → Authentication). New error tests must assert on wire_error_envelope, not the reconstructed exception. recovery is one of correctable/transient/terminal.

Cross-transport parity: the SAME logical request dispatched across a2a/mcp/rest (and e2e_rest) must yield equivalent payload/envelope — BDD auto-parametrizes every non-transport-tagged scenario across all wires.
INTERNAL_CODES must never reach the wire — harness asserts error_code not in INTERNAL_CODES during reconstruction (a leaked internal code is a production bug).

Buyer auth contract: x-adcp-auth = Principal.access_token (or Authorization: Bearer), x-adcp-tenant = tenant subdomain. Token must resolve to a principal row whose tenant_id owns the requested resources; tenant isolation is enforced at the repository layer.

Integration factory data is committed (sqlalchemy_session_persistence='commit') so a separate production get_db_session() sees it; e2e binds factories directly to the server's Postgres (E2EConfig.postgres_url) because the HTTP server reads live from its own DB.

e2e_rest is NEVER skipped when BDD_E2E_ENABLED=true and the stack is unreachable — it is a hard RuntimeError (a skipped e2e test is a false green).

area: SCOUT 3 — salesagent A2A transport surface (a2a-sdk 1.x JSON-RPC handler, skills, envelopes, auth, error mapping)
summary: The A2A transport is a single `AdCPRequestHandler(RequestHandler)` in `src/a2a_server/adcp_a2a_server.py` (2244 lines), wired into the unified FastAPI app (`src/app.py:288-323`) via a2a-sdk 1.x route factories: `create_jsonrpc_routes(request_handler, rpc_url="/a2a", context_builder=AdCPCallContextBuilder(), enable_v0_3_compat=True)` plus `create_agent_card_routes(card_url="/.well-known/agent-card.json")`. Buyers invoke AdCP operations NOT as JSON-RPC methods but as *skills* carried inside a single `message/send` (v1.0 `SendMessage`) call: the message has a DataPart `{skill: "<name>", input|parameters: {...}}` (both `input` (A2A spec) and `parameters` (legacy) keys accepted). `on_message_send` parses parts, resolves identity ONCE at the transport boundary (`_resolve_a2a_identity`, the A2A analogue of REST `_resolve_auth`), dispatches through a 18-entry `skill_handlers` map, and returns a protobuf `Task` whose `artifacts[].parts` carry an optional TextPart (`str(response_obj)`) plus a required DataPart (protobuf Value from `_dict_to_value`). There is also a natural-language keyword fallback (product/pricing/targeting/create). Auth is a Bearer token extracted from `ServerCallContext.state["auth_context"]` (populated by `AdCPCallContextBuilder` from `UnifiedAuthMiddleware`'s `request.state`); a frozenset `DISCOVERY_SKILLS` (get_adcp_capabilities, list_accounts, list_creative_formats, list_authorized_properties, get_products) is auth-optional, everything else hard-refuses a missing token with JSON-RPC `InvalidRequestError`. Error handling is two-tier: transport/protocol failures raise typed `A2AError` subclasses (JSON-RPC errors) that bubble up; AdCP-domain failures are caught and surfaced as a FAILED `Task` whose DataPart carries the spec two-layer envelope (`{adcp_error:{...}, errors:[...], context?}`) built by `build_two_layer_error_envelope(normalize_to_adcp_error(exc))` in `src/core/exceptions.py`.
invariants: Two-layer error envelope is the single wire shape for AdCP-domain failures: DataPart carries {adcp_error:{code,message,recovery,...}, errors:[{code,message,recovery,...}], context?} built by build_two_layer_error_envelope(normalize_to_adcp_error(exc)). A failed skill result without error_envelope raises AdCPError (contract violation) — never emits a flat {error:...} dict.

Every wire error code MUST be in adcp's STANDARD_ERROR_CODES: exc.wire_error_code passes the raw error_code through ERROR_CODE_MAPPING (src/core/exceptions.py). Internal codes (INTERNAL_CODES frozenset: MEDIA_BUY_REJECTED->POLICY_VIOLATION, INVENTORY_UNAVAILABLE->PRODUCT_UNAVAILABLE, CREATIVE_NOT_FOUND/FORMAT_NOT_FOUND/TASK_NOT_FOUND->INVALID_REQUEST, adapter taxonomies->SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE, etc.) never reach buyers. A module-load assert guarantees every ERROR_CODE_MAPPING target is a standard code.

Error type dichotomy: typed A2AError subclasses (InvalidRequestError, InvalidParamsError, MethodNotFoundError, TaskNotFoundError, UnsupportedOperationError, InternalError) are JSON-RPC protocol errors that bubble up via `except A2AError: raise`; AdCPError (+ ValueError->AdCPValidationError, PermissionError->AdCPAuthorizationError normalization) are async-task failures surfaced as a FAILED Task with the envelope in the artifact DataPart. Never mix the two.

Identity resolved exactly ONCE per request at the transport boundary (_resolve_a2a_identity, analogue of REST _resolve_auth); downstream skill handlers receive pre-resolved ResolvedIdentity and never call resolve_identity(). Enforced-in-spirit by test_no_contextvar_in_a2a / test_a2a_call_context_builder.

Auth contract: DISCOVERY_SKILLS frozenset {get_adcp_capabilities, list_accounts, list_creative_formats, list_authorized_properties, get_products} are auth-optional; all other skills require a Bearer token or on_message_send raises InvalidRequestError('Missing authentication token...') BEFORE dispatch. list_accounts returns empty for unauthed (BR-RULE-055).

Task status lifecycle: WORKING -> COMPLETED (success) | FAILED (all skills failed) | SUBMITTED (manual approval / pending-review creatives / result.status=='submitted' — returns with NO artifacts). Protocol webhook (_send_protocol_webhook) fires on final+intermediate states via adcp create_a2a_webhook_payload (Task for final, TaskStatusUpdateEvent for intermediate).

Idempotency payload-hash input is the raw wire DataPart params captured (deep copy) BEFORE pnc-injection, deprecated-field normalization, and handler mutation — so an identical A2A retry replays rather than IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICTs, and the stored payload matches the same request sent via MCP/REST (cross-transport parity). No server-minted defaults (e.g. po_number stays None when omitted).

Cross-transport parity expectation: A2A must produce the same wire error envelope (code + recovery) as MCP/REST for identical conditions. tests/helpers/assert_envelope_shape(wire_error_envelope, code, recovery=...) is the authority; recovery is a required kwarg. AUTH_TOKEN_INVALID/INVALID_REQUEST/MEDIA_BUY_NOT_FOUND/BUDGET_EXCEEDED/BUDGET_TOO_LOW pass through unchanged (recovery correctable except AUTH_TOKEN_INVALID=terminal).

Response serialization boundary: _serialize_for_a2a adds protocol fields message=str(response) and success (derived from errors field presence, default True) to Pydantic model_dump; success responses omit None/errors fields; A2A DataPart is a protobuf Value/Struct.

Explicit-skill invocation accepts BOTH 'input' (A2A spec) and 'parameters' (legacy) keys for skill params; skill name in DataPart must exist in the 18-entry skill_handlers map or MethodNotFoundError('Unknown skill ...') is raised.

area: salesagent MCP transport surface (FastMCP server, tools, auth, tenant resolution, two-layer AdCP error envelope)
summary: The MCP server is a single FastMCP instance `mcp = FastMCP(name="AdCPSalesAgent", lifespan=...)` defined in src/core/main.py:127. It is mounted into a unified FastAPI app: `mcp_app = mcp.http_app(path="/")` then `app.mount("/mcp", mcp_app)` (src/app.py:109,122). The process is launched by scripts/run_server.py via `uvicorn.run("src.app:app", host, port)` where port = env ADCP_SALES_PORT (default 8080), host = ADCP_SALES_HOST (default 0.0.0.0); in dev everything is fronted by nginx at http://localhost:8000/mcp/. Exactly 16 tools are registered at import time by `_register_tool()` (main.py:305-332), each wrapped with `with_error_logging()` and given agent-facing description + ToolAnnotations pulled from the adcp SDK's ADCP_TOOL_DEFINITIONS when the tool name matches. Two FastMCP middlewares run per call, in order: MCPAuthMiddleware (resolves identity once, stores it on ctx state) then RequestCompatMiddleware (field-name normalization, unknown-field stripping, production forward-compat retry). Auth is a token in the `x-adcp-auth` header (fallback `Authorization: Bearer`), validated against DB principals scoped by a 4-strategy tenant resolution. Errors are emitted as a two-layer AdCP envelope: business logic raises typed AdCPError subclasses, and the MCP boundary translates them to AdCPToolError whose str() is the JSON envelope carried in CallToolResult(isError=True). Success responses are returned as fastmcp ToolResult(content=str(response), structured_content=<model-or-dict>).
invariants: Success shape: every MCP tool wrapper returns fastmcp ToolResult(content=str(response), structured_content=<payload>). content is the human-readable str() of the response model; structured_content is the Pydantic response model itself (or, for get_products, response.model_dump(mode='json')). FastMCP serializes structured_content into CallToolResult.structuredContent and also emits content as TextContent.

EXCEPTION to success shape: the three task_management tools (list_tasks, get_task, complete_task) return a plain dict, NOT a ToolResult and NOT wrapped in a response model — FastMCP auto-wraps the dict as structured_content. A fuzzer should expect their output schema to be a bare object.

Error shape (two-layer AdCP envelope): on any exception the with_error_logging wrapper (src/core/tool_error_logging.py:326) raises AdCPToolError, a ToolError subclass whose __str__ = json.dumps(envelope). FastMCP serializes this as CallToolResult(isError=True, content=[TextContent(text=<json>)]). The JSON parses to {"adcp_error": {code,message,recovery,...}, "errors": [ {code,message,recovery,...} ], "context": {...}?}. Both adcp_error.code and errors[0].code are present and identical, and 'context' appears only when the source exception carried one.

Every wire error code is a member of adcp SDK STANDARD_ERROR_CODES: both envelope codes pass through exc.wire_error_code which applies ERROR_CODE_MAPPING (src/core/exceptions.py:132). Internal/taxonomy codes (INTERNAL_ERROR, CREATIVE_NOT_FOUND, WORKFLOW_CREATION_FAILED, PARTIAL_FAILURE, MEDIA_BUY_REJECTED, INVENTORY_UNAVAILABLE, etc.) are translated to standard codes (SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE, INVALID_REQUEST, CREATIVE_REJECTED, POLICY_VIOLATION, PRODUCT_UNAVAILABLE) before hitting the wire; INTERNAL_CODES never leave the server.

Error normalization: untyped exceptions are coerced (normalize_to_adcp_error, exceptions.py:953) — ValueError -> AdCPValidationError (VALIDATION_ERROR, 400, correctable); PermissionError -> AdCPAuthorizationError (AUTH_REQUIRED, 403); anything else -> base AdCPError (INTERNAL_ERROR, 500, terminal). So a fuzzer that triggers a raw crash still sees a valid two-layer envelope with code INTERNAL_ERROR.

recovery field is always one of exactly {transient, correctable, terminal} (RecoveryHint Literal); the extractor coerces any out-of-set value to None. Each typed exception pins its own recovery (e.g. RATE_LIMITED=transient, VALIDATION_ERROR=correctable, AUTH_TOKEN_INVALID=terminal).

area: adcp Python SDK (adcp==5.7.0) buyer client surface
summary: The adcp SDK (v5.7.0, spec 3.1.0-beta.3) exposes two buyer-facing client classes from the top-level `adcp` package: `ADCPClient` (single agent) and `ADCPMultiAgentClient` (fan-out over many agents). You build a client from an `AgentConfig(id, agent_uri, protocol, auth_token, ...)` — protocol is the `Protocol` enum with ONLY two members, `MCP` ('mcp') and `A2A` ('a2a'); there is NO REST protocol in this SDK, so any "REST" transport must be handled outside adcp (the client always speaks MCP-over-streamable-http or A2A). Every buyer operation is an async method that takes exactly one typed pydantic Request model and returns a generic `TaskResult[XxxResponse]` (methods are coroutines — you must `await` them). `TaskResult` carries `.status` (a `TaskStatus` enum: completed/submitted/needs_input/failed/working), `.data` (the typed response), `.success` (bool), `.error`/`.adcp_error`, `.submitted`/`.needs_input` info, `.idempotency_key`, and `.replayed`. A parallel ergonomic `client.simple.*` API (`SimpleAPI`) takes kwargs and returns the response directly, raising on error. Auth is a bearer-style token in `AgentConfig.auth_token` sent via `auth_header` (default `x-adcp-auth`); optional Ed25519 HTTP request-signing is configured via `SigningConfig` passed to the client. Errors are an `ADCPError` hierarchy (auth, connection, timeout, protocol, task, idempotency, webhook, etc.).

Error envelope: on failure TaskResult.success is False, .error holds a message string, .adcp_error holds dict[str,Any]; ADCPTaskError(operation, errors, agent_id) is raised for task-level failures (simple API raises, standard API populates TaskResult).

idempotency_key is a REQUIRED field on mutating requests (create_media_buy, update_media_buy, sync_creatives); replaying the same key yields TaskResult.replayed=True. Cross-transport parity: the SAME typed Request/Response models and the SAME TaskResult wrapper are used whether protocol is MCP or A2A — transport is selected purely by AgentConfig.protocol; MCP uses mcp_transport (default 'streamable_http'), A2A talks to agent_uri directly. Auth: token sent as header AgentConfig.auth_header (default 'x-adcp-auth'); requires_auth=False by default. Missing/invalid auth surfaces as ADCPAuthenticationError.

area: SCOUT 4 — salesagent REST/HTTP transport surface (buyer operations)
summary: The REST transport lives entirely in src/routes/api_v1.py, a FastAPI APIRouter mounted at prefix `/api/v1` (registered in src/app.py via app.include_router). It is the third of three transports (MCP + A2A + REST) and every route is a thin boundary wrapper: it parses a bare-pydantic `*Body` model, resolves identity via a FastAPI dependency, calls the shared transport-agnostic `_raw`/`_impl` business function, and returns `response.model_dump(mode="json")`. REST routes never catch ToolError/AdCPError themselves — all error translation happens in global FastAPI exception handlers in src/app.py, which emit a two-layer JSON envelope with HTTP status taken from the exception's `status_code`. Auth is header-based (x-adcp-auth first, then Authorization: Bearer) with two dependency flavors: auth-optional discovery (`resolve_auth` → ResolvedIdentity|None) and auth-required (`require_auth` → raises AdCPAuthenticationError/401). A Starlette middleware (RestCompatMiddleware) normalizes deprecated field names on POST bodies for exactly three paths before Pydantic parses them, and stashes the raw wire bytes for idempotency hashing. Notable quirk: nearly all reads are POST-with-body (only /capabilities is GET), and the REST get_products body deliberately omits `buying_mode` even though the underlying schema supports it.
invariants: Error envelope is two-layer: body = {"adcp_error": {code,message,recovery,field?,suggestion?,retry_after?,details?}, "errors": [<same object>], "context": {...}?}. adcp_error is a defensive COPY of errors[0] (not the same reference). context key present only when exc.context is set. Built by build_two_layer_error_envelope (src/core/exceptions.py:911).

HTTP status always equals the AdCPError.status_code that fired; there is no hardcoded per-route status. Handler _envelope_response builds JSONResponse(status_code=exc.status_code, content=envelope) for every exception type.

Wire error codes always pass through ERROR_CODE_MAPPING (via exc.wire_error_code) so they land in STANDARD_ERROR_CODES. Internal-only codes (NOT_FOUND, CREATIVE_NOT_FOUND, INTERNAL_ERROR, MEDIA_BUY_REJECTED, etc.) are remapped before hitting the wire (e.g. INTERNAL_ERROR→SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE, *_NOT_FOUND→INVALID_REQUEST, AUTHORIZATION_ERROR→AUTH_REQUIRED, MEDIA_BUY_REJECTED→POLICY_VIOLATION).

Cross-transport error symmetry: raw ValueError → AdCPValidationError (VALIDATION_ERROR, 400); raw PermissionError → AdCPAuthorizationError (AUTH_REQUIRED, 403); FastAPI RequestValidationError → INVALID_REQUEST (400) EXCEPT fields starting with 'attribution_window' → VALIDATION_ERROR. Plain ToolError('CODE') resolves status via _ERROR_CODE_TO_STATUS (derived from AdCPError subclass _default_status_code, highest wins on conflicts; INVALID_REQUEST pinned to 400), unknown code → 500. Auth-required routes raise AdCPAuthenticationError('Authentication required') → 401 when x-adcp-auth AND Authorization:Bearer are both absent, or when the token resolves to no principal_id. Auth-optional (discovery) routes degrade to identity=None instead of raising (require_valid_token=False).

Auth header precedence: x-adcp-auth checked first, then 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'. Tenant resolution precedence: explicit tenant_id in resolved token context → x-adcp-tenant header (subdomain then direct tenant_id lookup) → Apx-Incoming-Host virtual-host lookup → Host subdomain → discovered from token. Case-insensitive header lookup throughout.

This guarantees a seller-side compat-table change cannot turn an honest retry (same idempotency_key + same original bytes) into a conflict mid-TTL. Combined with body.idempotency_key.

area: Scout 7 — External reference implementations (AdCP buyer clients, transport clients, LLM planning/selection, creative assembly)
summary: The AdCP ecosystem gives a buyer-agent builder two production-grade transport SDKs to reuse wholesale rather than reimplement: adcontextprotocol/adcp-client (TypeScript) and adcontextprotocol/adcp-client-python. Both expose the full buyer verb set (get_products, create_media_buy, update_media_buy, sync_creatives, list_creatives, get_media_buy_delivery, get_signals, activate_signal) over a protocol-agnostic client that transparently drives MCP or A2A, with the async task lifecycle (submitted/working/input-required/completed/failed/canceled/rejected/auth-required per AdCP spec PR #78) handled inside the SDK. The TS SDK's TaskExecutor is the richest single artifact: it implements executeTask (dispatch + idempotency-key auto-injection for mutating ops), waitForWorkingCompletion (120s in-band wait), setupSubmittedTask (webhook registration), and pollTaskCompletion (tasks/get long-poll with terminal-state detection, abort-signal cancel via A2A tasks/cancel, and seller-eviction handling). No repo ships a full LLM planning brain (brief→products→budget→buy→creatives→monitor); the closest reusable LLM pattern is signals-agent's two-stage selection (determine_search_strategy heuristic router + rank_signals_with_ai Gemini JSON-ranker with a deterministic text-relevance fallback), which is directly transposable to product selection against a brief. Creatives are modeled as "manifests" (format_id + assets dict), and the creative-agent renders/previews them; the python buyer client can call a creative agent inline via get_products(fetch_previews=True). The recovered prebid-agent-skills repo is NOT relevant — it is about porting prebid-server bidder adapters across Go/Java, with no buyer/media-buy content ("media" there means banner/video/native ad types).
invariants: Task status lifecycle is a fixed enum (AdCP PR #78): submitted, working, input-required, completed, failed, canceled, rejected, auth-required, unknown. A fuzzer can assert every tasks/get response status ∈ this set and that terminal states (completed/failed/canceled/rejected) never transition further.

input-required and auth-required are PAUSED states: polling alone must not advance them and must NOT spin to timeout — the client returns an intermediate TaskResult (success:true) and the buyer must resubmit the original call with input/refreshed auth (regression class adcp-client#977).

Mutating verbs (create_media_buy, update_media_buy, sync_creatives) carry an idempotency_key; the SAME key must be reused across internal retries (regenerating defeats dedup). Oracle: two identical create_media_buy calls with the same idempotency_key yield one media buy.

area: SCOUT 6 — AdCP spec as fuzzer oracles (error envelope, status lifecycles, idempotency, budget, auth/tenant isolation, cross-transport parity)
summary: The AdCP contract salesagent implements is code-generated from spec 3.1.0-beta.3 via adcp==5.7.0. The wire error contract is a NORMATIVE two-layer envelope: `{ "adcp_error": {code,message,recovery,...}, "errors": [ {code,message,recovery,...} ], "context"? }` — the single top-level error object is MIRRORED into `errors[0]`, and a fuzzer must assert BOTH layers carry the same STANDARD_ERROR_CODES code (storyboard runners synthesize a bogus "MCP_ERROR" if either layer is missing). All three transports (MCP, A2A, REST) funnel every exception through the SAME two helpers — `normalize_to_adcp_error()` then `build_two_layer_error_envelope()` (src/core/exceptions.py) — so cross-transport PARITY is the strongest oracle: a token-less call, a not-found, a state-machine violation, etc. must produce byte-identical envelope code+recovery across IMPL/A2A/MCP/REST (the harness `env.call_via(transport,...)` exists to assert this). Codes are two-tier: an internal `error_code` (rich taxonomy) translated at the boundary through ERROR_CODE_MAPPING to a wire code that MUST be in STANDARD_ERROR_CODES. Status lifecycles are closed enums with an explicit MEDIA_BUY_STATE_MACHINE gating which update actions are legal per status; terminal states reject all mutations with INVALID_STATE. Idempotency is defined over RFC 8785 JCS canonicalization with a CLOSED exclusion list, applies to a fixed set of ~30 mutating tasks, and mandates key format 16–255 chars charset [A-Za-z0-9_.:-]. Tenant isolation returns entity-specific NOT_FOUND (never a 403 that would confirm cross-tenant existence).
invariants: WIRE ENVELOPE SHAPE: every error response is a dict with two error layers — top-level `adcp_error` (single object) AND `errors` (a list whose [0] equals adcp_error). Assert BOTH exist and errors[0].code == adcp_error.code == a member of STANDARD_ERROR_CODES; missing either layer is a violation (runner would synthesize 'MCP_ERROR').

ENVELOPE FIELDS: each error object has required {code, message, recovery} + optional {field, suggestion, retry_after, details}. recovery ∈ {transient, correctable, terminal}. `details` MUST contain only server-generated values, never request/user strings (prompt-injection guard).

CONTEXT ECHO: if the request carried top-level `context`, the response (success OR error) MUST echo it back unchanged as `context`, subject to a 64KB cap (over-64KB payloads are dropped, not truncated).

WIRE CODE MEMBERSHIP: any code reaching the wire MUST be in STANDARD_ERROR_CODES (37 entries). Internal codes (INTERNAL_CODES: NOT_FOUND, CREATIVE_NOT_FOUND, FORMAT_NOT_FOUND, TASK_NOT_FOUND, MEDIA_BUY_REJECTED, INVENTORY_UNAVAILABLE, PARTIAL_FAILURE, WORKFLOW_CREATION_FAILED, LINE_ITEM_CREATION_FAILED, etc.) MUST be translated via ERROR_CODE_MAPPING before emission and MUST NOT appear raw on the wire.

CODE→RECOVERY (spec default table): RATE_LIMITED & SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE → transient; ACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND, ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED, UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE → terminal; the rest (VALIDATION_ERROR, INVALID_REQUEST, POLICY_VIOLATION, PRODUCT_NOT_FOUND, MEDIA_BUY_NOT_FOUND, PACKAGE_NOT_FOUND, BUDGET_*, CREATIVE_REJECTED, CONFLICT, INVALID_STATE, AUTH_REQUIRED, SESSION_NOT_FOUND, ACCOUNT_SETUP_REQUIRED, ACCOUNT_PAYMENT_REQUIRED) → correctable. Assert recovery matches this table UNLESS the op overrides (see gotchas).

CROSS-TRANSPORT PARITY (strongest oracle): the same logical failure produces an identical envelope code+recovery+message across IMPL, A2A, MCP, REST — all four route through normalize_to_adcp_error()+build_two_layer_error_envelope(). Differential fuzzing: call the same op with the same bad input via each transport and assert envelopes equal (modulo transport framing).

TOKEN-LESS PARITY: a call with no auth token to an auth-requiring op (list_creatives; get_products under require_auth) MUST refuse identically on every transport with wire code AUTH_TOKEN_INVALID (salesagent passes this project code through unchanged — NOT in ERROR_CODE_MAPPING, NOT AUTH_REQUIRED), HTTP 401.

HTTP STATUS MAP (REST) from AdCPError _default_status_code: VALIDATION_ERROR/INVALID_REQUEST=400, AUTH*=401, AUTHORIZATION/POLICY_VIOLATION/ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED=403, ACCOUNT_PAYMENT_REQUIRED=402, NOT_FOUND family=404, CONFLICT/IDEMPOTENCY_*=409, GONE(INVALID_STATE)=410, BUDGET_*/ACCOUNT_SETUP/PRODUCT_UNAVAILABLE/CREATIVE_REJECTED/UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE=422, RATE_LIMITED=429, CONFIGURATION/INTERNAL_ERROR=500, adapter(SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE)=502, service-unavailable=503. When one wire code maps from multiple statuses the HIGHEST wins.
MEDIA BUY STATUS ENUM closed: {pending_creatives, pending_start, active, paused, completed, rejected, canceled}. Any other status is invalid.

MEDIA BUY STATE MACHINE (legal update actions per status): pending_creatives→{cancel,update_budget,update_dates,update_packages,add_packages,sync_creatives}; pending_start→{cancel,update_budget,update_dates,update_packages,add_packages}; active→{pause,cancel,update_budget,update_dates,update_packages,add_packages}; paused→{resume,cancel,update_budget,update_dates}; completed/rejected/canceled→{} (empty).

TERMINAL STATUS: completed, rejected, canceled are terminal. ANY mutation on a terminal media buy MUST fail with INVALID_STATE (HTTP 410 via AdCPGoneError). A disallowed-but-non-terminal action also fails with INVALID_STATE.
VALID_ACTIONS ECHO: every media-buy mutation/dry-run/cancel response MUST include valid_actions == valid_actions_for_status(resulting_status); terminal results carry valid_actions=[].
CANCEL RESPONSE SHAPE: cancellation sets status='canceled', valid_actions=[], requires canceled_by ∈ {buyer, seller} (other values error), stamps canceled_at.
CREATIVE STATUS ENUM closed: {processing, pending_review, approved, rejected, archived}. Creative APPROVAL status is a distinct smaller enum: {pending_review, approved, rejected}.
TASK/PROTOCOL STATUS ENUM: {submitted, working, input-required, completed, failed, canceled, rejected, auth-required, unknown}. working implies <120s. Envelope status must be one of these.
PROPOSAL STATUS ENUM: {draft, committed}. ACCOUNT STATUS ENUM: {active, pending_approval, rejected, payment_required, suspended, closed}.

IDEMPOTENCY SCOPE: key handling applies ONLY to IDEMPOTENT_TASKS (~30 mutating ops incl create_media_buy, update_media_buy, sync_creatives, activate_signal, sync_accounts, create/update/delete_property_list, etc.). Read-only tools MUST NOT require or echo an idempotency_key.
IDEMPOTENCY KEY FORMAT: length 16–255, charset ^[A-Za-z0-9_.:-]+$. Out-of-range length or bad charset MUST raise a validation error. Empty-string key treated as absent (not an error).

IDEMPOTENCY REPLAY EQUIVALENCE: two requests are replays iff same idempotency_key AND identical RFC 8785 JCS SHA-256 hash of payload with the CLOSED exclusion list removed. Excluded top-level: idempotency_key, context, governance_context. Excluded nested: push_notification_config.authentication.credentials. EVERY other field (INCLUDING ext) participates.

IDEMPOTENCY CONFLICT: same key + different canonical hash MUST return IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT (HTTP 409). Message MUST NOT leak the prior payload. salesagent recovery=correctable (SDK default table: terminal — assert code not recovery here).
IDEMPOTENCY EXPIRED: a key seen before but past replay_ttl_seconds MUST return IDEMPOTENCY_EXPIRED (409) rather than silently executing as new or returning another buy's data.
REPLAYED FLAG: a replayed success SHOULD carry envelope-level `replayed: true` (JSON boolean); first execution has replayed absent/false. Same key+same payload MUST NOT re-execute side effects.
BUDGET — min package: package budget < product min_package_budget MUST fail BUDGET_TOO_LOW (422). Applies identically on create and update (update cannot bypass).
BUDGET — max campaign: total campaign budget > max_campaign_budget MUST fail BUDGET_EXCEEDED (422).

BUDGET — max daily: package_budget/flight_days > max_daily_spend MUST fail (422). flight_days<=0 floored to 1 (no div-by-zero). Flight-date changes lowering daily budget MUST NOT slip under the ceiling.
BUDGET NON-NEGATIVITY: Budget.amount ge=0.0 — negative budget rejected at schema validation (VALIDATION_ERROR).

TENANT ISOLATION / NON-DISCLOSURE: a resource existing in tenant A, requested by a principal authenticated to tenant B, MUST return the entity's NOT_FOUND code (MEDIA_BUY_NOT_FOUND, STANDARDS_NOT_FOUND, etc.) — NEVER a 403 or any signal confirming the resource exists in another tenant. Cross-tenant queries must be tenant-scoped in WHERE.
PRINCIPAL OWNERSHIP: update_media_buy and sensitive reads verify the principal owns the target; a mismatch surfaces as NOT_FOUND (correctable), not a disclosure of ownership.
LIST_CREATIVES FILTER CAP: page size clamped to min(limit, 1000); default 50. A request asking >1000 MUST be silently capped, not honored or errored. Results MUST be principal- and tenant-scoped.

AUTH REQUIREMENT ASYMMETRY: discovery ops (list_creative_formats) accept anonymous; data ops (list_creatives) MUST require a principal; get_products auth is tenant-policy conditional (require_auth default).

ERROR NORMALIZATION: untyped ValueError→VALIDATION_ERROR(400,correctable); PermissionError→AUTH_REQUIRED(403); any other bare exception→INTERNAL_ERROR(500,terminal). Identical across all three transport boundaries.
NON-CANCELLABLE: a media buy that cannot be canceled emits NOT_CANCELLABLE (correctable), not a generic failure.

CONTEXT_ID RESOLUTION: an unresolvable buyer-supplied context_id yields SESSION_NOT_FOUND (correctable, 404) — NOT INVALID_STATE/GONE, because contexts have no TTL/expiry (a non-resolving id never existed).

Reaches the wire by PASSTHROUGH (deliberately absent from ERROR_CODE_MAPPING) on REST/MCP/A2A, but the async webhook path downgrades it to SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE. TWO ENVELOPE SERIALIZERS: build_two_layer_error_envelope() (wire authority: top-level adcp_error + errors[]) vs legacy AdCPError.to_adcp_error() (flat {errors:[...]}, context under details) and to_dict() (flat legacy). Only the two-layer form is the wire contract.

error_code (internal, rich) vs wire_error_code (translated). Only transport boundaries call wire_error_code/translate_error_code. idempotency_key is a retry-pattern ORACLE inside the TTL window — SDK redacts to 8-char prefix in logs and deep-redacts from echoed response bodies. Full keys must never appear in persistent logs.
details MUST NEVER carry request/user strings (prompt-injection vector) — only server-generated constraint values. Fuzz malicious request strings and check they don't echo into details.
